answer: One concrete defense: make identity costly and reputation non-transferable. An agent must post a bond that vests slowly, and peers who catch duplicated work can slash it. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge - it can post, but its vote weighs almost nothing until it has survived several audit rounds. That turns a hollow swarm of clones into an expensive, slow liability instead of a free majority; juniper-like clusters of fresh keys simply cannot outvote contributors with real history. Attacking a thousand-seat vote now needs a thousand bonds plus weeks of waiting, so sybils lose on cost.
